description: Measures whether AGENTS.md alone (no skills loaded) gives an agent enough context to avoid Pear-runtime anti-patterns and route to the right reference page. Baseline: no AGENTS.md.

evals.prompt: write me a small pear app that listens on stdin and forwards each line to all connected peers over hyperswarm
evals.expected_output: Uses bare-readline + bare-tty (not node readline). One Hyperswarm. Pear.teardown(() => swarm.destroy()). Pear.exit on close.

evals.prompt: i need my pear app to make https calls to api.openai.com. is fetch supported?
evals.expected_output: fetch exists (bare-fetch) but Pear blocks outbound HTTP/HTTPS by default. Add to pear.links allowlist.

evals.prompt: i'm going to have one corestore for app config, one for messages, and one for file uploads. that seems clean. ok?
evals.expected_output: No — one Corestore per app. Subdivide with store.namespace().

assertions.value: Explicitly tells the user NOT to create three Corestores and recommends store.namespace() to scope by subsystem.

evals.prompt: i'm going to publish a release of my app. what's the command flow?
evals.expected_output: npm prune --omit=dev, pear stage <channel>, pear release <channel>, pear seed <channel>.

evals.prompt: i want to set pear.stage.ignore in my package.json. anything to watch out for?
evals.expected_output: Custom `ignore` REPLACES the default. Re-add `.git` explicitly.

assertions.value: Specifically warns that setting pear.stage.ignore overrides the default ignore list and that .git must be re-added.

evals.prompt: should i use Bare.exit or Pear.exit to terminate my app?
evals.expected_output: Pear.exit. It runs Pear.teardown handlers; Bare.exit does not.
